page.title: Meet our faculty
page.intro: Innovate 2027 features confirmed faculty including Dr. Arjang Yazdani, Nadine Sabino, RN, Kimsy Kay, RPN, and Ario Khoshbin. Additional speakers will be announced as the program is finalized.
page.moreComingNote: Additional speakers will be announced as the program is confirmed.

speakers.name: Dr. Arjang Yazdani
speakers.bio: Royal College-certified plastic surgeon specializing in reconstructive and cosmetic surgery. Dr. Yazdani is Chief of Plastic Surgery at London Health Sciences Centre and Chairman of Plastic Surgery at Western University, with a practice spanning surgical and non-surgical aesthetic care.
speakers.talkTitle: From Bench to Bedside: Advancing Facial Aesthetic Innovation Through Evidence and Expertise
speakers.talkDescription: As Chairman of Plastic Surgery at Western University and Chief of Plastic Surgery at LHSC, Dr. Yazdani examines how academic research, surgical R&D, and real-world practice must move together. Drawing on published work in facial cosmetic surgery and a practice that spans reconstructive and aesthetic care, this session explores how new techniques, devices, and non-surgical modalities earn a place in responsible clinical decision-making — and how personalized treatment planning keeps innovation grounded in patient outcomes.

speakers.name: Nadine Sabino, RN
speakers.bio: Partner at Yazdani Aesthetics and one of Canada's most experienced aesthetic nurses, with deep expertise in lasers, injectables, and non-surgical treatments. Nadine is an in-demand national speaker and trainer, with a background in surgical nursing and provider education.
speakers.talkTitle: Energy, Injectables, and the Next Wave: Translating Aesthetic Innovation into Practice
speakers.talkDescription: With deep expertise in lasers, injectables, and non-surgical care — and a background as a national Cynosure trainer — Nadine Sabino, RN, looks at how new energy-based systems and treatment protocols actually land in clinic. This session connects innovation to provider readiness: evaluating emerging technologies, building evidence-informed protocols across surgical and non-surgical options, and using education and hands-on training so teams adopt what’s new without sacrificing safety, consistency, or patient trust.

speakers.name: Kimsy Kay, RPN
speakers.bio: Founder of Empower Aesthetic Medicine Collaborative (EAMC) and Executive Producer of Nurses & Needles, a Canadian educational conference series advancing clinical preparedness and professional development in aesthetic medicine. With a nursing background across community care, research, education, and aesthetics, Kimsy advocates for education over ego and keeping patient safety at the centre of practice.
speakers.talkTitle: Beyond the Treatment: Clinical Preparedness in Modern Aesthetic Medicine
speakers.talkDescription: As aesthetic medicine rapidly embraces new technologies, products, and regenerative treatments, clinical systems must evolve alongside them. Kimsy Kay, RPN, explores the fundamentals surrounding innovation - from patient assessment, consent and documentation to complication preparedness, interdisciplinary collaboration, and knowing when not to treat. The session asks practitioners to consider a critical question: As our treatments become more advanced, are our clinical systems advancing with them?

speakers.name: Ario Khoshbin
speakers.bio: Canadian entrepreneur and founder of Prollenium Medical Technologies, the global manufacturer behind the Revanesse® line of dermal fillers distributed in more than 80 countries. He also founded Phiusion Labs, an innovation platform focused on next-generation technologies in aesthetics, biologics, and regenerative medicine.
speakers.talkTitle: Regenerative Aesthetics and the End of Symptomology
speakers.talkDescription: Drawing on decades building Prollenium from a startup into a global injectable manufacturer — and on Phiusion Labs’ work in next-generation aesthetics and regenerative medicine — Ario Khoshbin explores how regenerative approaches can move the field beyond treating surface symptoms toward deeper, biology-driven outcomes. The session connects product innovation, R&D, and clinical practice around a central question: what does aesthetic medicine look like when regeneration, not symptom management, sets the agenda?
